elements.element: Trigger: obligation applies on expiry or termination
elements.evidence: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason"
"TrueLink shall (a) at Client's request, provide transition assistance"
"return to Client all Client Content and other Client data"

elements.element: Return in a standard machine-readable format

elements.evidence: "within 30 days after such expiry or termination"
"(c) thereafter delete such Client Content and data from its systems"
"certify such deletion to Client in writing"
"transition assistance for up to 6 months" exceeds 90 days
"within 30 days after such expiry or termination, return to Client all Client Content"

reasons: The inserted Section 14a supplies every atomic element of the preferred position: expiry-or-termination trigger, up to 6 months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of all Client Content and data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days after expiry or termination, and deletion followed by written certification.

The deterministic check flagging the 30-day return as absent appears inaccurate; the operative text expressly states "within 30 days after such expiry or termination, return to Client all Client Content and other Client data".

The request condition ("at Client's request") attaches only to transition assistance, not to the data return, deletion or certification obligations, so the mandatory post-termination return is preserved.

Minimality holds: the Agreement had no exit mechanics, and a single concise new section is the least intrusive fix; no existing sentence, term, renewal mechanic or termination-notice provision was altered.
Intent preserved: the clause uses existing defined terms (Client, TrueLink, Client Content) and introduces no contradiction with Sections 13 or 14.
